sources.entry: SurrealDB - A scalable, distributed, collaborative, document-graph database, for the realtime web. [![Open-Source Software][oss icon]](https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb)

summary.one_liner: SurrealDB is a multi-model database written in Rust that combines document, graph, relational, time-series, geospatial, key-value and search data in one engine, with realtime queries and built-in permissions.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a single Rust binary that can run embedded in an app, in the browser via WebAssembly, at the edge, as a single self-hosted node, or as a distributed cluster. It supports ACID transactions, record links and typed directed graph edges, and schema-full or schema-less tables with computed fields, events and unique indexes. Querying is done through SurrealQL, with REST and JSON-RPC over WebSockets, and the README says GraphQL is "coming soon". Live queries push data changes to clients, and row-level permissions control access, with user authentication supporting a backend-as-a-service style of use. It also lists full-text, vector and hybrid retrieval, geospatial GeoJSON types, embedded JavaScript functions (ES2020), and an MCP server for AI-agent integration.
use_cases: Building realtime collaborative apps with live query updates
Backend-as-a-service with end-user authentication and row-level permissions
Storing and querying graph relationships without JOINs
Embedding a database inside an application or edge device
Serving as a data layer for AI agents and knowledge graphs
Running a self-hosted or clustered database for web and mobile backends
how_to_run: docker run --rm --pull always --name surrealdb -p 8000:8000 surrealdb/surrealdb:latest start
docker run --rm --pull always --name surrealdb -p 8000:8000 surrealdb/surrealdb:latest start --log info --user root --pass root memory
notable: Multi-model: document, graph, relational, time-series, geospatial and retrieval in one query language
Graph edges and record links queried inline, avoiding JOINs
Row-level permissions defined in the database schema
Can run embedded, in the browser via WebAssembly, or as a distributed cluster
Built-in MCP server for LLM and AI-agent integration
caveats: Core database code is under the Business Source License 1.1, not an OSI open-source license; only libraries/SDKs and some core components are Apache 2.0 or MIT
GraphQL is listed as 'coming soon' in the README
A managed SurrealDB Cloud service is offered as a paid alternative to self-hosting
summary.license: Business Source License 1.1 for core database code (Apache 2.0 or MIT for libraries/SDKs and some core components)
